newsitem.title: USA: Entergy files Louisiana transition plan.
newsitem.headline: Entergy files Louisiana transition plan.

text.p: Entergy Corp said Thursday it filed a Transition to Competition Plan with Louisiana regulators that reflects the company's planning for competition in the electric power business.
Entergy said its proposal protects residential, small business and industrial customers from the threat of higher rates if some large industrial customers leave the system.
However, the company's statement gave no details on how this would be accomplished.
The utility filed a similar plan in Mississippi last month and plans filings in Arkansas and Texas this fall.
Entergy said the plan was filed with the Louisiana Public Service Commission, is for both Entergy Louisiana Inc and Entergy Gulf States Inc's Louisiana operations.
A primary feature of the transition plan is that customers who continue to receive their electricity from Entergy would see no change in their rates during the transition period.

Customers who remain connected to Entergy's electric facilities, but receive their electricity from another source -- and in reality, these are expected to be only some large industries -- would continue to pay their share of costs.

Entergy said its proposal also includes a base rate freeze that would last seven years, as well as separate provisions for Entergy Louisiana and Entergy Gulf States' Louisiana operations to completely write down nuclear investments in seven years, or about one-fourth the time currently scheduled.
For customers of Entergy Gulf States, the seven-year period would cover investment in the River Bend unit. For Entergy Louisiana, the seven-year period would cover investment in the Waterford 3 unit.
